narr: An upper-level disturbance interacting with a stationary frontal boundary draped across central Illinois triggered clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening of May 19th. Some of the cells produced flash flooding and hail as large as ping pong balls near Long Creek in Macon County, while others caused isolated flash flooding in parts of rural Douglas County.
ev: Water was flowing across the road in the 2200 block of Esther Avenue due to 1 to 3 inches of rain falling in a short amount of time.
A flowing creek washed out 200 feet on both sides of a culvert on North County Road 1965 East between East County Road 700 North and East County Road 800 North southwest of Murdock.
lsr: Video relayed by broadcast media of watter flowing quickly across the 2200th block of S Esther Ave.
